correctness.rationale: For a prescribed pattern on three distinct vertices, the restricted character expansion has constant q−3, three linear and three quadratic terms of magnitude at most 2, and a cubic sum of magnitude at most 2√q (squarefree cubic). This gives 8N≥(√q−5)(√q+3)>0 for q>25. In four EF rounds a fresh response must match at most three distinct vertices and can be supplied by this property (pad to three if needed); old vertices are matched to their counterparts. For the six allowable boundary representatives the five formulas are of rank ≤4, including U of prefix ∃∃∃∀ and the finite conjunction E of prefix ∀∀∀∃. Independent exact finite-field checks give vectors 00100,10100,11100,11000,11010,11011 for orders 5,9,13,17,25,29, respectively; this separates every class and gives the sharp in-family bound. Enumerating isomorphism types of four-vertex induced subgraphs gives exact set equality within each of the pairs 13/17 (9 types) and 25/29 (all 11 types). Replay: branches/46ca6823-dcda-4e1f-b9ac-10c1f69f70ac/paley_independent.py and independent_output.txt. The finite test is not evidence for the infinite tail by itself. originality.rationale: The prior 3-e.c. threshold, and consequently the upper-tail EF equivalence, are not new. Neither the known threshold nor the inspected nearby Resultary conclusions resolve all small orders or give the two same-four-vertex-age pairs with explicit alternating-quantifier separators. The pass credits that complete classification and finer distinction, subject to the primary access limitation below.
residual_risks: The 1993 primary text might contain additional explicit small-order extension profiles not described in the consulted secondary passage.
This is a bounded evidence comparison, not a claim of historical priority or a bound among arbitrary graphs.

value.rationale: A complete plain first-order rank-four partition of this canonical graph family is useful for comparing finite models. The two equal-induced-age pairs give concrete sharp examples where quantifier alternation distinguishes models missed by tests for induced four-vertex graphs; the finite classification is more informative than repeating the prior 3-e.c. cutoff.
